profiles.meeting_scenario: A coordination meeting between the analytics platform team and the developer productivity team at a mid-sized SaaS company. They are preparing a data-informed retrospective activity for the next sprint review cycle by mining GitHub, Jira, and CI repository data from one product squad, Checkout Experience. The immediate context is that the developer productivity team has already prototyped repository metrics, while the analytics platform team owns the shared event pipelines and dashboard templates used in internal facilitation sessions. The agenda is to align on what dataset will be produced for the retrospective, how it will be packaged for the facilitator, what time window it should cover, and what level of validation is needed before handing it off. The expected outcome is apparent agreement on the interface between teams: Priya will provide the extracted metrics package and Leo will plug it into the retrospective dashboard and facilitator brief before Friday's prep deadline.

members.name: Priya Natarajan
members.expertise: Repository mining, CI/CD telemetry, internal engineering analytics
members.background: Priya built internal scripts that aggregate GitHub pull request activity, review latency, deployment frequency, and Jira issue transitions for engineering effectiveness initiatives; she usually works directly with engineering managers and is used to shipping analysis as notebook outputs plus CSV extracts.
members.private_state: She wants to minimize rework by reusing the prototype extraction job she already has, avoid getting pulled into dashboard implementation details, and make sure the retrospective artifact looks credible enough that leadership will approve a broader rollout.
hidden_assumptions: When someone asks for the retrospective dataset for Sprint 42, they mean the exact Jira sprint window as configured for the team board, even if code activity spills slightly outside that range.
A handoff to another internal technical team can reasonably be a CSV bundle plus a short README because they can transform it as needed.
A metric is validated if spot checks on a few known pull requests and tickets match the repository records; formal reconciliation against dashboard totals is unnecessary for a pilot.
The Checkout Experience team refers to the single active application repo plus its linked Jira board, because that is how managers usually discuss the squad's work.

members.name: Leo Martinez
members.expertise: Internal dashboards, stakeholder reporting, data product handoffs, retrospective facilitation support
members.background: Leo maintains the internal retrospective dashboard framework and facilitator packet templates used by delivery leads; he often coordinates across data producers and nontechnical facilitators, so he optimizes for plug-and-play artifacts and consistent definitions across teams.
members.private_state: He wants a clean deliverable that can drop into the existing dashboard without manual cleanup, avoid any last-minute facilitator confusion, and keep the artifact consistent with the cross-team reporting conventions already used by operations leadership.
hidden_assumptions: When someone says Sprint 42 for retrospective prep, they mean the operational reporting week set used in the dashboard, which extends through the Sunday deployment cutoff around the sprint end.
A handoff for dashboard use means a structured JSON export conforming to the existing schema, plus stable field names and chart-ready labels, not raw analysis files.
Validated means the numbers line up with the existing engineering insights dashboard totals closely enough that a facilitator will not see mismatches during the session.
Checkout Experience includes the customer checkout frontend repo and the shared checkout-service repo because facilitators discuss the squad's process across both codebases.

misalignment_points.surface_form: Both agree to use 'Sprint 42' or 'last sprint' as the reporting window
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: Priya will extract issues and PR activity bounded by the Jira Sprint 42 start and end timestamps on the team's board.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: Leo expects the dashboard package to use the reporting window associated with Sprint 42, including activity through the Sunday deployment cutoff after the sprint ends.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Using the sprint name sounds fully specific in an Agile context, so neither expects a hidden alternate calendar convention behind the same phrase.

misalignment_points.topic: What the Checkout Experience team includes
misalignment_points.surface_form: Both talk about pulling metrics for 'Checkout Experience'
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: Priya scopes the analysis to the squad's main application repository and its Jira board because that is the standard unit for her extraction job.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: Leo assumes the retrospective view should include both the frontend repo and the shared checkout-service repo because facilitators discuss process friction across the full feature area.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: The team name is a natural shorthand and both have legitimate organizational reasons for treating it as a complete scope, so the boundary difference remains invisible.

misalignment_points.surface_form: Both agree Priya will 'send the dataset' or 'hand over the metrics package'
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: Priya plans to send CSV files and a README generated from her notebook workflow, expecting Leo to map fields into the dashboard.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: Leo assumes the handoff will be a schema-compliant JSON payload or table export already shaped to the dashboard contract so he can ingest it directly.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: In cross-team coordination, 'dataset' and 'metrics package' sound like sufficient interface language, and each person defaults to the artifact format normal in their own workflow.

misalignment_points.surface_form: Both agree the metrics should be 'validated before the facilitator sees them'
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: Priya considers the pilot validated once a few representative PRs, deployments, and tickets have been manually spot-checked against source systems.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: Leo believes validation means the final package reconciles with the existing engineering dashboard totals well enough that no visible discrepancies appear in the retrospective materials.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both are sincerely quality-conscious and use the same reassuring term, but the standard of proof differs in a subtle way tied to their downstream responsibilities.
